verdict: Lend selectively to Visakhapatnam port-linked service and logistics borrowers with contracted cargo and short receivable cycles; avoid pure coal-handling capex plays and any group with large disputed tax claims.
title: Visakhapatnam Ports & Port Services: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
Visakhapatnam port moves bulk cargo — coal, iron ore, fertiliser, containers — and the money is made by handling it, not owning it. **The cash engine is throughput times tariff, minus fuel, labour and equipment hire.** VPA handled 91.17 MMT in 2025-26 and 46.14 MMT in April–September 2026, up 7% year-on-year, with average vessel waiting time down 37% to 0.45 hours [3]. Faster turnaround means more trips per asset, so a stevedore or handler with fixed equipment earns more on the same capital. **Ask every borrower for their tonnage handled per month and their per-tonne realisation; if realisation is falling while tonnage rises, they are buying volume with price.**

## Where value and cash sit
Value sits in the berth relationship and the equipment; cash sits in the receivable. **The working-capital cycle is the whole credit story here.** A rated peer in the group shows an operating cycle of 51 days in FY24, with debtor days elongating [9]; another port peer improved receivables from 81 days in FY22 to 57 days in FY23 [11]. So when a proposal lands, check debtor days against these benchmarks; if a Visakhapatnam borrower shows debtor days above 60, ask which customer — port authority, trader or shipping line — is holding the cash. **Capex is heavy and lumpy: tugs, cranes, barges.** Fund it with long-tenor debt matched to the asset, never with working capital limits.

## What has changed now
Local news is positive and recent: infrastructure strengthening at Visakhapatnam port is flagged as a key priority [1], and VPA marked record throughput with modernisation and digital upgrades [3]. Peer results confirm volume momentum — Adani Ports reported Q2 FY27 profit up 16.5% to ₹3,622 crore on revenue of ₹11,340 crore, with 60% EBITDA margin [5][6]. **But a research note flags cost inflation offsetting volume growth for logistics and ports in Q2 FY27 [7].** So the sector is growing top-line while margin is squeezed; price the risk accordingly. Note the rating reports [8][9][10][11] are undated or old — treat their ratios as reference, not current.

## Who to pursue, how to grow safely
**Pursue stevedores, clearing-and-forwarding agents and equipment hirers with contracted volumes from VPA or established traders.** Avoid single-customer coal handlers and any group with large disputed service-tax claims — one peer group carries claims of ₹197 crore, about 23% of net worth [9]. Structure: cash-flow-based limits, monthly stock-and-receivable statements, escrow of port receivables where possible. **Take every month: tonnage handled, debtor ageing, and confirmation of the berth or contract.**

## Early-warning signs
- Vessel waiting time rising from 0.45 hours [3] (monthly) -> ask for berth schedules; if delays persist two months, cut limit.
- Debtor days crossing 60 [9][11] (monthly) -> freeze fresh disbursal until collection plan is filed.
- Tonnage flat while fuel costs rise [7] (quarterly) -> reprice or reduce exposure.
watch: Rises above 0.45 hours for two months -> ask for berth schedule and trim limit
Crosses 60 days -> freeze fresh disbursal until collection plan filed
Flat or falling while costs rise -> reprice or reduce exposure
Any claim above 20% of net worth -> decline or seek personal guarantee
